title: The Bill Reminder
intro: A reminder lands about your electricity bill. After a day of threats, you trust nothing.
But some messages are real. Mirage loves it when you stop trusting the honest ones.

notify.text: Your bill is due on the 28th

subject.text: Your October bill is due on the 28th

p: . It matches your usual monthly use.

p.text: Pay in your Brightgrid app or account, as usual.
Nothing is wrong. This is only a reminder.

foot.text: Your account number ends in 0412 · We never ask for your full card number or PIN by email.

addr.label: The company's real address
addr.lens: It comes from bills@brightgrid.energy, the company's own domain.
addr.why: A matching domain is good evidence, so also look at what it asks.

subject.label: A plain subject
subject.why: Calm subjects are typical of real bills.

name.label: Uses your name
name.why: It proves little alone, but fits a real account.

amount.label: A normal amount
amount.why: You can compare with past bills.

date.label: A clear due date, not today
date.lens: Due on the 28th, with time to pay.
date.why: Honest reminders give you time. Scams threaten tonight.

pay.label: Pay as usual
pay.lens: It sends you to your own app or account.
pay.why: Pointing you to your own account is what honest companies do.

nothreat.label: No threat
nothreat.why: Honest reminders do not threaten you.

foot.label: Partial account number, and a safety line
foot.lens: It shows only the end of your account number, and says it never asks for card numbers or PINs.
foot.why: Real companies warn you about scams.

actions.label: Open my Brightgrid app and pay the bill as usual

go_ahead.line: The app showed the same £62.40, due on the 28th, matching your usual use. You paid in two taps.

ignore.line: Nothing bad happened today. But a bill ignored too long can bring real late fees. Checking was the better move.

block_report.line: That was a real bill reminder. When every message looks like a scam, the real ones get lost too.
block_report.mirageSays: If you trust nothing, I win anyway.

what_if.block_report: It matched your usual bill, gave you time, sent you to your own account and threatened nothing. That calm is what real messages look like.
what_if.ignore: Ignoring was safe. Recognising a real message is the skill: it asks for nothing secret and matches something you know.

golden_rule: A real bill reminder matches your usual bill, gives you time and sends you to your own account. A scam threatens tonight.

quick_check.q: What made this bill reminder honest?

options.text: It matched your usual bill, gave time and sent you to your own account

quick_check.explain: Your usual amount, time to pay and no threat are the real signs.

hints.nudge: What is this message actually asking you to do?

rows.k: Do real utilities demand same-day payment?

rows.v: In your own app or account
